symbols.name: _materialize_kms_descriptor
symbols.docstring:
Persist a KMS key identifier as a static JSON descriptor for inspection.

Key material is never fetched; only the identifier the user supplied is recorded
so the scan pipeline has a concrete local artifact to attribute findings to.
Failures are logged with the (truncated) identifier and re-raised as
ValueError so the scan endpoint returns a real 422 message instead of an
empty 500 with no server-side explanation.

symbols.name: _materialize_container_descriptor
symbols.docstring:
Persist a container image reference as a static JSON descriptor.

Registries are never pulled and containers are never started; only the
image reference the user supplied is recorded so the scan pipeline has a
concrete local artifact to associate CBOM findings with. Uploaded
`docker save` archives still take the deep-inspection path (layers, files,
packages, libraries, configuration). Failures are logged and re-raised as
ValueError so the caller returns a real error message.

The resolved Path is the *filesystem input for the scanner*. The original
user-facing artifact (identifier, URL, filename) is preserved separately
via ``_canonical_target_source`` — resolution never rewrites the request
into a fake repository representation.

symbols.name: _check_locator_shape
symbols.docstring:
Routing-table lookup plus target-specific locator-shape checks.

Shared by the lightweight pre-queue validation and the full background
build so both reject the same inputs with identical messages.

symbols.name: _validate_scan_locator
symbols.docstring:
Fast synchronous pre-queue check for POST /api/v1/scans.

Resolves the locator and verifies route + file/dir shape WITHOUT hashing
file contents or constructing Asset/Target records — the full
``_build_request`` (read_bytes + sha256 + HMAC derivations) runs in the
background worker. This keeps queue-accept latency flat across target
types and sizes so the browser's POST timeout never fires on large
binaries while a prior scan holds the SQLite lock.

symbols.name: _build_request
symbols.docstring:
TARGET NORMALIZATION: user input → target-specific input → SCAN REQUEST.

Pipeline: USER INPUT → TARGET-SPECIFIC INPUT (upload bytes, KMS
identifier, image reference, git URL, local path) → TARGET NORMALIZATION
(this function: resolve a scanner-readable locator while preserving the
original target in ``target_source``/``artifact_metadata``/asset tags) →
SCAN REQUEST (RunRequest) → TARGET-SPECIFIC SCANNER (see
``SCANNER_ROUTING``) → CRYPTOGRAPHIC FINDINGS → CBOM → RISK/MOSCA →
DASHBOARD. Normalization never destroys the original target type.

symbols.name: _persist_scan_status
symbols.docstring: Persist a lightweight lifecycle state before a full RunResult exists.

symbols.name: _run_scan_in_background
symbols.docstring: Execute one isolated scan outside the HTTP request lifetime.

symbols.name: _run_full_scan_in_background
symbols.docstring:
Full async scan worker: resolves repo/tarball THEN runs the scan.

This is what create_scan() submits so that the blocking _build_request()
call (which includes tarball download for GitHub/GitLab repos) happens OFF
the HTTP request thread.  The provisional_scan_id that was already returned
to the client is used as the authoritative run_id throughout, bypassing the
orchestrator's internally-derived ID.

symbols.name: create_scan
symbols.docstring:
Accept a scan request and return immediately with a provisional scan_id.

The blocking work (tarball download, AST parsing, risk scoring) is off-loaded
to a background thread via _run_full_scan_in_background so the browser's
AbortSignal.timeout on the POST never fires.  The client polls GET
/api/v1/scans/{scan_id} until the run settles.

docstring:
Versioned, conservative taxonomy for per-finding cryptographic risk.

Taxonomy 1.0.0 separates classical cryptographic condition from quantum
applicability. It only classifies named algorithms, lifecycle states, and
parameters covered by the explicit rules below. Unmatched or under-specified
algorithms remain UNKNOWN; absence of a match is not evidence of weakness.

docstring:
Static adapters for non-tree discovery targets.

All adapters operate on caller-provided local bytes. They never clone, pull, execute,
or mutate a target. Archive extraction is bounded and rejects traversal paths.

symbols.name: _parse_descriptor_document
symbols.docstring:
Return the parsed descriptor dict when bytes are a KMS/container reference doc.

``None`` for anything else (real archives, manifests, binaries). Descriptors
are the small JSON documents QRYPTON itself materializes from a bare user
identifier (KMS ARN, image reference); they contain no inspected bytes.

symbols.name: LibraryDependencyScanner
symbols.docstring:
Library/dependency target scanner: manifests, packages, wheels, JARs.

Same static archive/token engine as :class:`ExtendedStaticScanner`; the
distinct name routes LIBRARY targets to their own scanner and keeps the
original target type visible through normalization into the CBOM.

symbols.name: ContainerImageScanner
CloudKmsScanner
symbols.docstring:
Static cloud-KMS identifier and supplied-descriptor scanner.

It never authenticates to AWS, Azure, or GCP and never makes a provider API
call. Key material is neither requested nor accessed.

symbols.name: _descriptor_observation
symbols.docstring: Build the honest reference observation for a descriptor document.

symbols.name: _descriptor_fallback
symbols.docstring:
Honest fallback for KMS/container reference descriptors.

Bare identifiers (AWS ARN, Azure URL) contain no algorithm tokens, so
the token engine is structurally silent. A reference descriptor still
proves a crypto-relevant asset exists — record it as a library-type
observation, never as a fabricated algorithm claim.
